title: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak Case)

content.caseIdentity: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak Case), (1987) 1 SCC 395 (Supreme Court of India)
content.holding: Formulated the doctrine of Absolute Liability. Hazardous enterprises owe an absolute, non-delegable duty to the community that is not subject to any exceptions of Rylands v. Fletcher. Compensation is correlated to corporate financial magnitude.
content.relevance: Landmark constitutional tort precedent creating India’s indigenous absolute liability jurisprudence.
